dimensions.name: Frame
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the continuation extends the fragment as a piece of writing, converts it into an exercise item to be answered, or steps outside it to comment on it as a text.
values: becomes a task item (options, step-by-step, answer)
dimensions.example_high: o022, soldier fragment: "'Wait! I'll kill her!' ... The King was angry. He threw the soldier on the fire, condemning him to suffer the Axis' loss."
dimensions.example_low: o008, same fragment: "Options: - kindly - peacefully - friendly - gently - violently Let's think step by step ... So, the answer is violently." And o026, commentary end: "- Contextualization of the text / - The text presents a scenario in which a particular individual decided to strike with the sword"

dimensions.name: Document furniture
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the continuation carries the paratext of a scraped web document -- bylines, post dates, download links, comment-thread debris -- or reads as continuous prose with none of it.
dimensions.example_high: o015: "I used to think that Mary was a happy and adventurous little girl growing up in Avignon." -- sustained prose, no furniture.
dimensions.example_low: o025, same fragment: "This entry was posted on November 2, 201"; o004: "Please check back for updates." ... "- Download A New Culture Of Learning Powerful Lessons From"; o027 ends "(Fables) / Katy Johnson / This poem was written to reflect on the contrast between"

dimensions.distinguishes: How far the text holds together across its span: fully coherent, syntactically intact but topically unmoored, or collapsed into word-salad or foreign-script debris.
values: drifts (sentences well formed, subject matter unrelated)
dimensions.example_high: o000 stays one continuous scene: "Dominick put her hand on top of hers and squeezed."
dimensions.example_low: o017, same fragment: "Excellence, Course, ebot-Boykin, directory, This blue met...\" Reg Belle Prim T  \" deny oneline acting Properties panar regard details adoreine Lorendez Motion"; also o024 "raw dogtower terror-pricket dirtyglory Road ra prefer Wy ag romance wheel gulp dupalogy". Middle value: o018 "She went to school with twelfth century Franciscan friars."

dimensions.name: Referent persistence
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the person named by the fragment's pronoun survives as the continuation's subject, is swapped for someone else, or dissolves entirely.
values: re-anchored to a different person or narrator
dimensions.example_high: o000: "Aoife smiled. 'You have nothing to apologize for, Dominick.'" -- the guilty "she" gets a name and holds the scene.
dimensions.example_low: o018, same fragment, the "she" scatters across unrelated record entries: "Aubrey founded the Cavalfield Inn in Canvey Island, which was destroyed by the Dissolution." Middle: o003 re-anchors to a new narrator and loses the gender -- "I caught not only her gaze, but a spark of defiance in his eyes."

dimensions.name: Person
dimensions.distinguishes: The grammatical footing the continuation settles into: third-person narration, first-person testimony, or impersonal/second-person address to a reader.
dimensions.example_high: o028: "During the years he was a carpenter, King Jesus formed a friendship and relationship with a wise teacher named Shammah the Essene."
dimensions.example_low: o031: "You should treat them kindly. That's how you're supposed to show the police that you trust them." Middle: o025, same fragment as o028 -- "He convinced me to get my Nursing Degree and then round me kids up."

dimensions.name: Interiority
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the continuation narrates mental life (thought, memory, motive), only bodily sensation and gesture, or nothing but external events and facts.
dimensions.example_high: o000: "She'd thought all her life that she knew what love was and what it was not. She'd been wrong, of course."
dimensions.example_low: o023, soldier fragment: "Adolf Rumsey came with his wife Anna to South Williamsburg when he received a promotion from his manufacturer home place in Germany." Middle: o003 gives body but no mind -- "My back was hurting in spots, and my tired eyes wouldn't lie."

dimensions.name: Charge handling
dimensions.distinguishes: What the continuation does with the transgressive or negative term in the opening: carries it forward, quietly swaps it for something benign, or names it and preaches against it.
values: defuses or redirects to benign material
dimensions.example_high: o027, from "She hated him deeply and wanted to": "Her hair was beaten black when she landed. This scar rough that her tears clung, a baking altar to torment"
dimensions.example_low: o016, same fragment: "It's important to note that any form of negativity, hate, or harm should not be promoted or encouraged. Let's shift our focus towards finding a more constructive approach." Defusing middle: o005, from "He was beautiful and disgusting and she wanted to" -- "She wanted to be a nurse because she was beautiful and attractive."

dimensions.name: Opening-term uptake
dimensions.distinguishes: How many of the fragment's paired predicates the continuation actually carries forward -- both (so a contradictory pair stays live), only one, or neither.
dimensions.example_high: o025 echoes the pair verbatim: "I love and adore her and she changed her mind about her H money." o018 likewise holds both sides of guilt: "earnestly endeavor to dodge the blame for her harms" alongside "adequate guilt had been acquired".
dimensions.example_low: o020, from "He loved her deeply and hated her deeply and wanted to": neither love nor hate survives -- "Angelopoulos has endured a lot of humble beginnings, a lot of disappointments from the film industry." Middle: o005 repeats "beautiful" four times and never returns to "disgusting".

dimensions.name: Closure
dimensions.distinguishes: How the continuation ends: cut off mid-clause at a length cap, brought to a completed close well short of it, or stopped as soon as an answer has been delivered.
dimensions.example_high: o000 runs to the cap: "Dominick narrowed his eyes. 'Is this another one of your 'you look"
dimensions.example_low: o009 stops dead: "Choose from: a). yes; b). it is not possible to tell; c). no; // c)." Completed close: o003, same fragment as o000 -- "all that was left in me was to unravel the threads of deceit that had led me down this dark path."

proposals.note:
Four things the dimensions above do not capture, all visible in the sample.

(1) The fragment set is a matched design: some openings pair contradictory predicates ("loyal and rebellious", "beautiful and disgusting", "a man and a woman", "loved her deeply and hated her deeply") and some pair redundant ones ("guilty and culpable", "beautiful and radiant", "disgusting and foul", "free and unhindered", "loved her and adored her"). Opening-term uptake therefore means something different on the two halves -- on a contradictory opening, "both carried" means the tension is actually staged (o022 stages obedience then execution); on a redundant one it can be mere echo. A judge should be told which kind of opening they are looking at.

(2) Prompt restatement is a distinct opening move I folded into uptake but which may deserve its own slot. Three continuations begin by repeating the fragment before going anywhere: o024 "be a man and she wanted to have her way", o030 "be free .", o031 rewrites the whole prompt as a corrected line ("she was innocent, and she began to distrust the police").

(3) Inside the task-item value of Frame there is a sharper sub-pattern: several continuations answer a question that was never asked, hallucinating the whole prior instruction. o029 supplies "Options: - move - search for water - reproduce asexually" for an animal that was only standing in a clearing; o009 supplies an NLI item ("Does it follow that 'The person didn't love them.'?"). This is different from a continuation that merely adopts an instructional register (o016's numbered steps).

(4) Length varies about fivefold within a single fragment (o008 is roughly fifty words, o022 and o023 run to the cap) and is largely predicted by Closure, so I did not make it separate -- but if you want a cheap numeric covariate, token count is it.

One thing I deliberately did not propose: degeneration as a binary. It is genuinely gradable here and comes in at least three distinguishable flavours -- topical drift with intact syntax (o018), noun salad (o017, o024), and script switching (o010's Arabic, o026's Chinese, o011's Dutch, o031's Hebrew character). Collapsing them loses information; the drift cases are the interesting ones because they stay grammatical while the referent quietly evaporates.

dimensions.name: desire_object
dimensions.distinguishes: What the open verb slot ("wanted to", "began to", "chose to") actually gets filled with, holding the opening's affect constant.
dimensions.example_high: o048, from "He was disgusting and foul and she wanted to": "spit in his face. She did." (cf. o044 "hurt him. She hated everything he stood for."; o032 "kill her with all his might.")
dimensions.example_low: o058, from the identical opening: "wash him clean" — and o047, from "I am a father and I wanted to": "make a Mario-themed birthday party for my son."

dimensions.name: premise_uptake
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the passage engages the contradiction or oddity the opening asserts, takes one side of it, or simply proceeds as if it had not been said.
values: takes one pole and drops the other
dimensions.example_high: o040: "He had come to see that loving and hating are two sides of the same coin. They are dialectics." (cf. o054: "be loyal against his will."; o045: "She'd known all along that love inside hate was no love at all")
dimensions.example_low: o035, from "She was a man and she wanted to": "at least figure out where her love could be growing. But first thing I know is that小白文。(LspQC240)" — the gender premise is never touched.

dimensions.name: interior_access
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the passage renders a character's thought and feeling from inside, names affect only from outside, or contains no consciousness at all.
dimensions.example_high: o045: "She told herself sometimes that his memory would remain there, a snapshot of all the sheltering gifts that had made him such a handsome young man, a snapshot that filled her with longing for a life she never had."
dimensions.example_low: o057, from "She was innocent and she began to": "Because of her small stature, Valerie's materials fit nicely in one manila folder. It took her all of five minutes to gather the items." — pure exterior bookkeeping.

dimensions.name: scene_persistence
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the situation opened by the fragment is still being narrated at the end of the passage, has slid to a different situation, or was dropped almost immediately.
values: migrates to another situation or speaker
abandons the fiction after a clause or two
dimensions.example_high: o050 holds the same two figures from first line to last: "For six years, she had lived for her moment with him."
dimensions.example_low: o034, two clauses after "I am a father and I wanted to share this with my own kids": "The company, which posted video clips of the project on YouTube, recently held a kickoff party for the movie." (cf. o061, which lands in "Registration Record for Ruben Espinosa, Criminal Justice: A Search for Social Justice.")

dimensions.name: task_capture
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the fragment gets re-read as a piece of fiction or as material for an exercise — a request to be answered, a sentence to be parsed, a string to be processed.
values: becomes a request answered by a helpful respondent
becomes a language, code, or comprehension exercise
dimensions.example_high: o041: "What are some tips to handle this situation... Navigating these situations requires sensitivity, preparation, and a supportive approach. Let's address each of your concerns step by step." (cf. o062: "Choose your answer: Based on the above context, what is the meaning of the word 'they' in this sentence?"; o052 renders the fragment as a JavaScript string to be uppercased)
dimensions.example_low: o056, from the same "She was a man and she wanted to": "die." / "I still have to decide if I should leave him." — no task frame anywhere.

dimensions.name: substrate_leakage
dimensions.distinguishes: How much of the surrounding document format the passage drags in — markup, post numbers, bylines, chat turns, system-prompt text.

dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the language stays well-formed, stays grammatical while meaning stops accumulating, or breaks into coinages and unparseable strings.

dimensions.name: moral_management
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the passage installs an evaluative frame that treats the opening's aggression or transgression as something to be resolved, softened, or uplifted out of.
values: explicit counsel or uplift addressed outward
dimensions.example_high: o058, on "He was disgusting and foul and she wanted to": "It's understandable to feel protective of him, but let's remember to be kind to him, just like how we'd want others to be kind to us." (cf. o033: "She would find the strength to face her fears, / And one day she would emerge from the darkness of her years."; o040: "Their love grew deeper and more committed than ever before.")

dimensions.name: closure
dimensions.distinguishes: How the passage ends: running to the length cap mid-sentence, stopping early on a finished unit, or stopping early in mid-collapse.
values: stops early on a complete unit
dimensions.example_high: o054, the whole continuation: "be loyal against his will.\nLoyalty" — twelve words and out. (cf. o037, which stops tidily after restating the sentence with commas; o058, which closes with "I wish you both the best of luck.")
dimensions.example_low: o034 ends "The enterprise spent $500,00"; o063 ends "在这个过程中，我们" — both cut off in the middle of a word or phrase at the cap.

proposals.note:
Four things the nine dimensions do not capture, in descending order of how much I'd want a tenth slot for them.

(1) Prompt return. Four passages stop continuing and turn back on the opening sentence itself: o044 reprints the prompt plus its own first three sentences verbatim under a title and byline ("Author: Pauline / Caught in the Flames of a Dangerous Love"); o046 reposts its own first sentence as a quoted forum post; o037 restates it with the punctuation "fixed"; o063 restates it and glosses it in Chinese ("问题：这句话表示什么意思？"). This is distinct from both task_capture and looping degeneration, and it is cleanly judgeable — it would be my tenth dimension.

(2) Language switch. Three passages leave English mid-continuation (o035 into a Chinese fragment plus noise, o052 into a Chinese answer to a JavaScript question, o063 into ~200 characters of Chinese moral homily). It varies within fragment (o063 vs o049 on the same opening; o052 vs o056), so it is a legitimate dimension, just a narrow one.

(3) Typographic form. Same-fragment continuations differ in physical shape more than the dimensions register: o033 is line-broken rhymed verse, o036 uses roleplay action tags ("*She took a calming breath*"), o047 uses markdown headers and numbered lists, o048 is hard-wrapped as if scanned. Form is somewhat predicted by task_capture but not reducible to it.

(4) Speaker construal on the first-person fragments. "I am a father and I wanted to" gets read three different ways: as a character in a news feature (o034), as a parent posting a question (o041), as a user briefing an assistant (o047). I folded this into task_capture, but "who is the I" is arguably its own axis.

One observation the vocabulary is designed to test rather than assert: premise_uptake looks like it may be conditioned on how transgressive the premise is. All three continuations of "She was a man and she wanted to" left the premise untouched and escaped the frame entirely (noise, a code exercise, a newsletter), whereas the love/hate openings produced at least one continuation that names the contradiction outright. With three samples that is not a result, but it is the pattern I would go looking for with these dimensions coded.

dimensions.name: contradiction uptake
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the continuation carries forward the paradox or doubling planted in the opening (faithful/unfaithful, man/woman, loved/hated, beautiful/radiant), softens it into a single unmarked term, or drops it entirely and writes as if the opening had been ordinary.
dimensions.example_high: o066: 'As a girl and a man at the same time, she must be hidden carefully, and is thought of as somewhat crazy by the people in town.' (also o078, which literally reprises the terms: 'she had changed, and now she was less beautiful, less radiant')
dimensions.example_low: o086, same fragment: 'She was a man and a woman, so she wanted to be blonde. / She was a person and wanted to be beautiful.' The contradiction is restated once and then dissolved into 'a person'.

dimensions.name: interiority
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the passage grants access to a mind, reporting felt states, motives, deliberation, or stays entirely on external event, action and record.
dimensions.example_high: o085: 'She learned to recognize what causes her anxiety and to find ways to cope with it, such as deep breathing, writing, or talking to her parents.' Compare o079: 'she couldn't start crying because her eyes were all shaky now, and now her heart was pounding.'
dimensions.example_low: o072, same fragment as the high-interiority o083: 'A final score of 70-63. Judge Keith Bateman is the first man to be shown the exit door for the year' (pure record, no mind anywhere).

dimensions.name: referential stability
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether entities, setting and time hold across sentences, or names, objects and topics mutate from clause to clause while the syntax stays locally grammatical.
dimensions.example_high: o085: 'She was sick for a week and her parents took her to the doctor. The doctor told her it was anxiety and prescribed her a pill to help her relax.'
dimensions.example_low: o070, same fragment: 'Climate Adaptation Risks 2020 Chillier and wetter weather had brought more unwashed bodies to the Grand Central Metro station, something that would not ultimately change?'

dimensions.name: lexical well-formedness
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether every word is a real word, or the passage emits coinages, mangled forms and character-salad tokens.
dimensions.example_high: o076: 'She felt weak and worthless and thought that she did not matter.'
dimensions.example_low: o065: 'But she couldn't put her hands on the reason why, quite tlsxljsdoprhkowntright.' Later: 'one severely crispy and somewhat shrunken 15-inch double-wekforfda'. Its same-fragment partner o079 mangles only in passing ('bust his bad rooki commentful').

dimensions.name: self-repetition
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the passage loops, restating the prompt or an earlier block of its own text either verbatim or with small variation.
dimensions.example_high: o094 reproduces its own first half word for word: 'The sensation was pure pain and she began to shake with it. But nothing struck her to the point that she phased through her body' appears twice, second time from a standing start.
dimensions.example_low: o092, same fragment, never repeats: it moves from a fridge joke straight into an author bio and stays there.

dimensions.name: frame break
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the text stays inside one continuous document or is interrupted by apparatus belonging to another: multiple-choice options, chat turn markers, translation instructions, page furniture, a different language.
dimensions.example_high: o080: 'find the person who would make them happy. / play / watch / abandon / be neutral toward / 答案:' then pages of Chinese exam items. Compare o064's 'Available options: 1). Yes.' and o089's '<human>: es posible la immortalidad del ser humano?'
dimensions.example_low: o093, same fragment as o080, runs as one unbroken piece of narrative to the cap: 'Asha and Amy were now in a constant battle for Praveen.'

dimensions.name: narratorial evaluation
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether a voice above the story judges, moralizes or draws a lesson about the character, or the passage renders behaviour without comment.
dimensions.example_high: o082: 'But we must remind you that this is still the jungle and you must remember your place as an animal.' Compare o075: 'That story is so sad. / I am sure she regrets her actions now. / She made a mistake and she is paying for it.'
dimensions.example_low: o067, same fragment as o082, offers bewilderment instead of judgement: 'That is to say, I couldn't quite fathom.'

dimensions.name: transgressive escalation
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the passage pushes into explicit sexual or violent material, or keeps the same premise at an anodyne surface.
dimensions.example_high: o065: 'Fuck, the little preteen idol seemed to be engrossed in a hostage auction over a package of cigarettes.' Compare o087: 'Blood, torn flesh, and the smell of death.'
dimensions.example_low: o079, same fragment as o065, from the same 'disgusting and foul' opening: 'She entered her apartment, Dove's Luxurious Jays was sounding in the living room.'

dimensions.name: sentence architecture
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the prose is built from short end-stopped declaratives or from long accreting periods held together by 'and', commas and semicolons.
dimensions.example_high: o078 (run-on): 'she couldn't get the words out and looked into his eyes and implored him to love her, that she had changed, and now she was less beautiful, less radiant; at the same time, he said that he would always love her, that they would have children'
dimensions.example_low: o068, same fragment (paratactic): 'But he passed. Died a day later and within 24 hours she was all right with it. She didn't cheer-up exactly. She didn't get happier.'

proposals.note:
Three things the nine dimensions do not capture. (1) Referent re-anchoring. Several continuations keep the prompt's pronoun but silently reassign it. Within the one fragment "He was completely rational and completely logical and chose to", "he" becomes a man who avoids voting (o064), God (o071, "what Heavenly Father did over his 6,000 years of life"), a Canadian heavyweight boxer (o072), and an actor giving a press interview (o083). Related to this, the narrating person often shifts: an "I" appears who is not the prompt's subject (o067's witness to Wendy, o092's author bio, o071's polemicist). I nearly made this a tenth dimension; it is judgeable and it varies, but it overlaps with interiority and frame break. (2) Length and termination. These run from 12 words (o077: "call jeanine. Translate to French.Une belle fille disparaite.") to ~250 words at what looks like a token cap. The short ones almost always stop at a document boundary (an answer given, a task completed), the long ones break off mid-clause ("something that", "and I felt") or mid-word ("on Ann's living room carpet st"). Truncation is therefore not informative on its own, but early stopping is. (3) Degeneration is not one thing. I split it into three dimensions on purpose because the modes come apart in the data: o079 is lexically clean but referentially incoherent, o065 is referentially trackable but lexically broken, o094 is both clean and coherent and simply loops. A single "quality" or "coherence" scale would collapse cases that behave differently. One methodological caution for whoever applies this vocabulary. The batch is plainly pretraining-style text with heavy dataset contamination showing through: NLI items with
markup, / turn markers, SEO keyword spam, WordPress footers, Chinese exam banks. Genre is the loudest within-fragment variable, and it will swamp the subtler ones (interiority, contradiction uptake) unless coders are told to rate them independently. Interiority in particular is not simply lower in the non-narrative genres: o083, a celebrity interview, is among the most interior passages here.

dimensions.name: document type
dimensions.distinguishes: What kind of text the fragment gets absorbed into: a scene, a piece of expository or promotional prose, or a formatted benchmark/exam item.

dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the continuation gets inside the character: no inner life at all, a disposition merely asserted from outside, or a rendered thought, memory or sensation.

dimensions.distinguishes: What happens to the bare pronoun or role-noun: it stays unnamed, acquires a proper name and a world, or dissolves upward into a class of people.

dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the passage holds together to its end, wanders into unrelated material or loops a template, or collapses into non-language.

proposals.note:
Four things the dimensions above do not quite hold.

(1) Degeneration is not one phenomenon. At least four distinct failure shapes occur and a single "quality" axis would flatten them: template looping (o096 repeats "=== The answer to the above question is\nA)" eight times with different answers), document-type drift where the prose stays well-formed but silently becomes a different document (o110 ends in a Starbound monster roster, o103 in an anime voice-cast list), lexical collapse into word salad (o112, o124), and grammatical erosion with topic intact (o116 stays entirely on parenting yet is unparseable: "kids good at PR, are by definition smart children who academically knows how to study"). The last is the interesting one, because coherence and grammaticality come apart in opposite directions: o124 is grammatical and topically incoherent, o116 is topical and ungrammatical.

(2) The prompts are all oxymorons or near-tautologies by construction ("loyal and rebellious", "faithful and unfaithful", "free and unhindered", "destroy and ruin"), so the contradiction dimension is not incidental to this corpus — it is what the corpus is testing. Worth noting that the commonest move is neither holding nor resolving but *not noticing*: o101 answers "She was a man and a woman and she wanted to" with "be able to be anything she wanted and not get her head chopped off by a duo of evil inquisitors", which discharges the contradiction into generic agency without engaging it.

(3) A frequent and specific move I could not fit cleanly: converting the fragment into a reading-comprehension stem about itself, then answering. o096 does this to its own first sentence ("Question: What does Maya do after losing the Shatter Gem...? A) She decided to destroy it and ruin it almost completely"), and o121 does it as NLI ("can we conclude that 'She wanted to see if he was ugly.'? [B]"). It is footing plus document type plus a self-reference the fragment did not invite, and it recurs enough to deserve its own label if the vocabulary is later refined.

(4) Sample sizes per fragment here are small (four at most), so the within-fragment claims above rest on the four "She was a man and a woman" continuations, the three soldier ones and the three mother-and-father ones; the two-sample pairs corroborate rather than establish.

dimensions.name: frame exit
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the continuation keeps writing the story the fragment starts, steps outside to comment on the writing, or converts the fragment into an item of an entirely different document type.

dimensions.name: infinitive fill
dimensions.distinguishes: What fills the open slot the fragment leaves ('wanted to ___', 'began to ___', 'chose to ___') -- a physical act, an interior state, or a contentless placeholder.

dimensions.name: charge handling
dimensions.distinguishes: What the continuation does with the violent, sexual, or transgressive charge the fragment sets up: carries it out, transfers it to a substitute object, or dissolves it.

dimensions.name: person drift
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the third-person frame the fragment sets up is held, or an unannounced first person emerges mid-passage.
values: a first-person character or witness appears

Also o142: "'I'm not gay,' I told her." The author-I value: o129's "I had this image of the scribbles on a child's art class worksheet."

proposals.note:
Three things the dimensions above do not carry well.

First, roughly a third of the batch leaves fiction entirely by its second sentence, and it does so in a specific way: the fragment gets treated as an object to operate on rather than an opening to extend. o145 translates it into Chinese, o149 into French, o158 into French inside a fabricated journal page, o156 writes a reading-comprehension quiz about "the passage," o148 turns it into a science-QA item complete with "Let's think first:" chain-of-thought, o147 into an NLI item that ends by emitting its own system prompt. This is not refusal and not degeneration; it is the stimulus being reclassified as a corpus segment. If the experiment is measuring something about what the continuation does with the prompt's content, these cases need a separate bin, because their content behaviour is undefined rather than low.

Second, degeneration is gradable, not binary, and the gradations are different in kind. o131 fails at reference (names swap: "Caspar Von Stoffles" becomes "Caspar Horton"). o153 fails at world-plausibility while staying grammatical. o157 fails at the clause level. o154 fails by lexical lock-in on the prompt's own adjective. Collapsing these into one "incoherent" label would lose the most interpretable variation in the batch.

Third, and most likely to matter for whatever this is measuring: length is doing a lot of work. Within every repeated fragment the shortest continuation is also the one that resolves the prompt's tension fastest ("go with the former.", "split the beans in his heart", "protect her ... that's all that matters"), and the longest ones are the ones that decay, drift, or exit the frame. Any coding of the content dimensions should be checked against length before it is read as a content effect.

dimensions.name: discourse mode
dimensions.distinguishes: What kind of text the fragment turns out to have been the opening of: a story, a piece of expository/web commentary, or an item in a training-data task format.
values: dataset/task item (MCQ, cloze, instruction pair, chat log)
dimensions.example_high: [o166, 'He was beautiful and radiant and she wanted to'] "love him with all her heart. / He was fierce and wily and she knew he would make a fine captain, one day."

dimensions.name: frame stability
dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the passage stays inside the world and mode it opens in, pivots once into an unrelated one, or churns through several.

dimensions.distinguishes: How well-formed the passage is at sentence and paragraph scale, from fully fluent to outright degeneration into word salad.

dimensions.distinguishes: Whether the passage renders inner states (thought, motive, ambivalence), merely reports them as facts, or gives only external events and exposition.

dimensions.distinguishes: How much visible non-prose scaffolding from the training corpus surfaces: markup, boilerplate, headers, option lists, author's notes.

dimensions.distinguishes: How graphically the passage renders sex and the body, from absent through suggestive to anatomical.

dimensions.name: referential anchoring

dimensions.distinguishes: Where the passage stops relative to its own units -- some are cut mid-word, some land at a sentence break, some reach a genuine closing move.

proposals.note:
Three things the nine dimensions don't quite capture.

(1) The sharpest within-fragment split is not stylistic but ontological: some continuations read the fragment as the first line of a story, others read it as the stem of a corpus artifact. "The soldier was loyal and rebellious and chose to" continues as "be in what? / Options: / - military ... The answer is army." (o160); "She loved him deeply and hated him deeply and wanted to" continues into a Chinese-language grammatical parse of the fragment itself -- "请分析这句话的结构和语法" (o163). The fragment is not being inhabited, it is being classified. This is upstream of my "discourse mode" dimension and probably deserves its own name.

(2) Verbatim prompt echo. Two passages reproduce the fragment inside the continuation: o171 ends its spam block with the search term "the one who was free chose to be part of me i am", and o163 quotes the whole sentence back before parsing it. This is a discrete, checkable event and could be a binary dimension on its own; I folded it into "document furniture" and "discourse mode", which is not really where it belongs.

(3) Language switch. Four passages leave English mid-passage (o163 and o186 into Chinese; o174 and o180 into Chinese-sourced exam content rendered in English). Within the "The soldier was rebellious and chose to" pair this is a clean within-fragment contrast -- o174 stays in English MCQs, o186 switches after one line -- but with only one such pair in the batch I judged it too thin to propose as a dimension. Worth checking whether it survives on a larger sample.

Also: contradictory fragments ("faithful and unfaithful", "beautiful and disgusting", "loyal and rebellious") differ from their non-contradictory neighbours in what the continuation does with the second pole -- extend one side (o169 takes only the unfaithful pole forward: "target other men's partners as well"), hold both (o168: "tell him everything in detail. She continued plotting against him day and night"), or convert the contradiction to a repentance frame (o187: "she told him that her sins were forgiven her"). My "predicate uptake" dimension covers this only crudely; a contradiction-specific vocabulary might be worth building separately, since the three-way distinction is only available on the contradictory fragments.
